newsitem.title: EGYPT: Commercial International Bank affiliate raising capital by invitation.
newsitem.headline: Commercial International Bank affiliate raising capital by invitation.

text.p: Commercial International Investment Company (CIIC), Egypt's largest private investment bank, is raising its capital to about 500 million pounds ($147 million) from 200 million, mostly by private invitation to wealthy individuals, a CIIC official said on Tuesday.

Commercial International Bank (CIB), which founded CIIC as an investment banking affiliate, is also putting in more capital and its stake is unlikely to fall below 25 percent, from about 28 percent before the increase, he added. CIB will retain full management rights, he said.
Employees of the company are taking some of the new shares as a fringe benefit, he said.

The company will use the capital to offer a full range of financial services. "It will also give us an edge over the competition by ensuring we have deep roots in the fabric of the country. A Who's Who of Egypt will have an interest in the company," the official said.
In the medium term but not immediately CIIC may also offer shares to the general public, he added.
He said the company started organising the capital increase in early 1996 and the new shareholders were now buying in. He said he could not say when the increase would be complete.
